mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown four consecutive weeks of improvement toward baseline (-74.7 to -64.3), reflecting a self-reinforcing recovery in shopping and leisure activity that will continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent any shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -74.7 to -64.3 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean over the last 28 days despite the four-week improving trend continuing unbroken.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily from 25.0 to 20.3, indicating reduced time spent at home. If RESIDENTIAL drops below 18 points above baseline, it signals a behavioral threshold where households resume discretionary out-of-home trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 25.0 to 20.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses below 18 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are improving together (-56.4 to -45.4 and -65.7 to -57.7 respectively), and their joint recovery amplifies commute-linked retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in every week of the snapshot
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue rising but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and WORKPLACES mobility are both recovering (-91.9 to -87.3 and -56.4 to -45.4), consistent with a loosening-restrictions policy regime; this combined policy easing signal should continue lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks only while the regime remains in loosening mode.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -91.9 to -87.3 and WORKPLACES from -56.4 to -45.4
failure_condition: The regime shifts to tightening (PARKS or WORKPLACES reverse and decline week-on-week) yet RETAIL_REC still rises, or the regime stays loosening but RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improvement is decelerating (gains shrinking each week), suggesting essential-trip demand is seasonally saturating; this plateau in baseline necessity travel caps additional discretionary retail growth, leading to flat or declining RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM weekly gains shrank from 3.0 to 6.4 to 1.2 points across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite continued deceleration in GROCERY_PHARM gains.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC weekly gains have decelerated from 4.6 to 4.0 points; if this deceleration continues and the weekly improvement falls below 3 points, consumer behavioral momentum will stall, producing lower mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week gain drops below 3 points after exceeding 4 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gain fell from 4.6 to 4.0 points between the last two weeks
failure_condition: Weekly RETAIL_REC gains drop below 3 points yet the mean over the next 28 days still exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improvement has slowed to only 0.7 points in the latest week; if transit week-on-week gains fall below 1 point, it signals a policy or capacity ceiling on transit throughput that will cap RETAIL_REC growth over the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improvement slowed to 0.7 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT gains stay below 1 point yet RETAIL_REC still rises over the following 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM are both recovering simultaneously, and their joint improvement reflects broad-based economic reactivation that compounds to lift RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would suggest, over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -56.4 to -45.4 and GROCERY_PHARM rose from -39.0 to -28.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM continue improving together but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed the prior 14-day mean.
